answer: A separately deployed process is a runtime/deployment unit: it can fail, be released, scaled and rolled back independently. A state-authority boundary is a data-ownership boundary: the place where a business invariant is finally enforced and authoritative state transitions are owned. They answer different questions and need not coincide: one deployable can contain several authority boundaries, and several processes can share one authority, so neither a process split nor a separate database automatically creates a state-authority boundary. Splitting processes for isolation is justified only when the acceptance contract, duplicate identity and state owner are well defined.
